en: 8. The Question of the Bow “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one part of the bow must be taken,’ which is that one part that must be taken?
“Just as a well-crafted bow, O King, when bent, bends evenly from tip to root, neither stiffening nor resisting;”
In the same way, Great King, a practitioner of yoga, a follower of the spiritual life, should neither bow down nor show hostility toward elders, juniors, those of middle standing, or equals.
This, Great King, is one quality of the bow that must be adopted.
And this was said, Great King, by the Blessed One, the God above Gods, in the *Vidhura-puṇṇaka Jātaka*:
Even a firm bow with a well-strung belly might cause a bamboo to tremble,
yet it would not turn against the grain.
"Let him dwell in the king's residence.
This is the eighth question, on the curved eyebrow.
